draft.title: Media and behaviour
card: Media includes TV, film, games and social media. Social media is online platforms where people share posts and respond to each other.
Social media can help people stay in touch with friends and family, and find others who share their interests.
People can judge themselves by comparing their lives, looks or success with what others post. Posts are often selected and edited, so the comparison can leave people feeling worse.
Some apps are designed to keep people scrolling, which can lead to addictive use. Media can also spread harmful norms, which are unhealthy ideas about how people should look or act.
draft.remember: Media can build connection, but it can also feed social comparison, addictive use and harmful norms.

opts: Ravi feels dull after seeing friends' holiday posts
Ravi video calls his cousin who lives overseas each week
Ravi joins an online group for people who love chess
Ravi finds he cannot stop scrolling even when he is tired
a.why: Social comparison is judging yourself against what others post, and Ravi does this with the holiday posts. Being unable to stop scrolling is addictive use, which is a different risk.
a.clue: Which person is measuring himself against others?

b.q: Priya's favourite influencer says that a very thin body is the only healthy one. Many followers start to believe this. What does this best show?
opts: Media causing addictive use of an app
Media making followers obey a direct order
b.why: The influencer is spreading an unhealthy idea about how people should look, and followers take it on. That is a harmful norm. Followers believing a message is not the same as being given an order.
b.clue: Focus on the unhealthy idea being spread.

a.best: Ravi feels dull after seeing friends' holiday posts
